issues.display_title: Issue #29: Show popup message close app
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Summary

Replace the previous behavior (which strictly blocked window close with a toast warning during active uploads or media ingest) with an interactive confirmation modal (CloseConfirmDialog).

When the user attempts to close the application while an upload or media processing task is in progress, a confirmation dialog appears warning that continuing will stop all running processes.

Behavior & Flow

  1. Trigger Condition:

    • Active uploads (isUploading && !isPaused) OR
    • Running media ingest / frame extraction (status === "running").
    • Note: Paused uploads do not block close (maintaining previous behavior).

  2. User Actions:

    • Keep Running / Cancel: Dismisses the modal; the application remains open and processes continue uninterrupted.
    • Quit and Stop Processes:
      • Sends cooperative cancellation (commands.cancelJob) to all active upload and ingest jobs.
      • Transitions modal to a non-dismissable waiting phase with an animated spinner and live accessibility announcement (aria-live="polite").
      • Polls backend job registry (commands.listJobs()) every 300ms until all target jobs are confirmed terminated and child processes (e.g. FFmpeg, ExifTool) are safely terminated.
      • Features a 10-second timeout safety valve to prevent hangs.
      • Once cleared (or upon timeout), programmatic window destruction (window.destroy()) closes the window cleanly without prompt loops.

Technical Implementation

  • Tauri Permissions: Added core:window:allow-destroy to src-tauri/capabilities/default.json to allow programmatic window termination.
  • Coordination Logic (src/app/lib/closeGuard.ts):
    • collectActiveJobIds: Aggregates active job IDs across upload and ingest stores.
    • cancelActiveJobsAndWait: Orchestrates dispatching cancellations and polling backend registry as authoritative source of truth.
  • State Machine Hook (src/app/hooks/useCloseGuard.ts):
    • Intercepts onCloseRequested from Tauri window API.
    • Implements re-entrancy prevention on confirm action and proper listener unmount cleanup.
  • UI Component (src/app/components/CloseConfirmDialog.tsx):
    • Built with Radix UI AlertDialog for focus trapping and accessibility.
    • Locks Escape key and outside dismissal during the stopping phase.
  • i18n Localization:
    • Added 5 new localization keys (close_confirm_title, close_confirm_description, close_confirm_quit, close_confirm_keep_running, close_confirm_stopping) across all 15 supported locales (en, de, da, es, fr, it, jp, nl, pl, pt, ro, ru, sk, sv, zh).
    • Cleaned up obsolete toast notification strings.

Verification

  • Unit tests added in src/app/__tests__/closeGuard.test.ts (8 tests passing).
  • pnpm test (all 81 unit tests passing).
  • pnpm lint (ESLint & Prettier passing).
  • pnpm build (TypeScript strict check & Vite bundle successful).
  • cargo check (Rust backend compiles cleanly with capability changes).

Demo

Summary

The map view fails to load and remains blank when running the packaged desktop application (production build), even though it displays properly during development.

User Impact

When opening a project, users cannot see the map preview, GPS route path, or camera positions/markers in the installed app.

What Happened

The map engine relies on a background helper (worker) to process and render map graphics. When packaging the app for release, this helper file was not included in the application bundle. As a result, the map was unable to start and showed a blank screen.

Expected Behavior

The interactive map should load and display routes, tiles, and markers consistently in both development and installed desktop builds.

issues.display_title: Issue #28: Impelement FPS Settings for video generation
issues.main_description_html:
Demo

﻿### Summary
When importing 360 videos to build street-level tours, extracting every single frame (e.g., 30+ frames per second) produces thousands of redundant images, consumes excessive storage, and significantly slows down the import process.

This feature introduces a Target FPS (Frames Per Second) setting in the import dialog, allowing users to choose how frequently frames are extracted from their videos before processing begins.

Key Capabilities

  • Convenient Presets: Quick one-click options for common frame rates:
    • 10 fps (Recommended / Default): Balanced speed and coverage for most street tours.
    • 5 fps: Faster extraction, ideal for slower-moving captures or smaller disk footprints.
    • 15 fps: Higher density captures for fast movement.
    • Original (No filter): Retains all source video frames (0 fps / unfiltered).
  • Custom FPS Input: Allows entering any custom value between 1 and 60 fps.
  • Clear Guidance: Helpful tooltips and text explaining the trade-offs between extraction speed and image density.
  • Drag-and-Drop Confirmation: Dropping a 360 video directly onto the app window opens a confirmation dialog where you can review and adjust the extraction FPS before starting.

issues.display_title: Issue #25: Implement drag/drop project/video on dashboard.
issues.main_description_html:
Demo

2026-09-16.09-28-25.mp4

﻿### Summary
Allows users to drag and drop video files directly onto the Street Builder window/dashboard to streamline the tour import process, removing the need to manually click through file picker dialogs.

Key Capabilities & User Experience

  • Full-Window Drag & Drop: Dropping a supported video file anywhere on the dashboard triggers the import workflow with visual drop-zone feedback.
  • Supported Formats: Automatically detects standard 360 video formats (.mp4, .mov, .m4v).
  • Format Guidance (Insta360 & GoPro): Dropping camera raw formats (.insv or .360) displays a clear guide on how to stitch/export standard MP4 files via Insta360 Studio or GoPro Player.
  • Pre-Import Confirmation & FPS Control: Opens a confirmation dialog displaying the file name, target project path, and an integrated FPS selector (presets: 5, 10, 15, Original, or custom 0–60) before frame extraction begins.
  • Safety & UX Safeguards:
    • Prevents accidental duplicate extraction if an ingest is already running for the same video.
    • Temporarily disables drop handling when other modal dialogs are active to prevent competing focus traps.
    • Informs the user when multiple files are dropped by selecting the primary valid video and alerting about extra files.

(Note: Currently handles video drag & drop for ingestion. Dragging existing project directories/manifests can be tracked as a follow-up enhancement).

issues.display_title: Issue #26: Analysis command line after drop video
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

When dropping a 360 video onto the dashboard (or performing other media/upload operations), a visible black terminal / command prompt window pops up and flashes or remains visible on screen while background tools execute.

This issue documents the analysis of why command prompt windows appear on Windows and tracks the solution to make all sidecar processes run silently in the background.

Problem Description

  1. Drop Video & Ingest: Immediately after dropping a video and confirming the ingest job, black console windows (for ffmpeg.exe, bolt42.exe, and exiftool.exe) visually pop up on Windows.
  2. Long Extraction Times: During frame extraction, the ffmpeg console window stays open on top of or behind the app window for the entire duration of extraction (seconds to minutes), interrupting user workflow.
  3. Other Operations: A similar brief flashing of console windows occurs during sidecar diagnostics probing, timeline strip generation, and EXIF tagging before tour upload.

Root Cause Analysis

In Windows, binary executables such as ffmpeg.exe, exiftool.exe, bolt42.exe, and ffprobe.exe are compiled with the Console subsystem (IMAGE_SUBSYSTEM_WINDOWS_CUI).

When a GUI application compiled with #![windows_subsystem = "windows"] calls standard child process spawning APIs (such as tokio::process::Command::new()) without an attached console:

  • The Win32 CreateProcessW API defaults to allocating a new console window (conhost.exe) for each console child process.
  • Redirecting stdin/stdout/stderr pipes does not suppress console window allocation.
  • To run child console processes silently, Windows requires the process creation flag CREATE_NO_WINDOW (0x08000000).

In the current codebase (crates/sb-core/src/media/sidecar.rs):

  • SidecarCommand::run_captured() and SidecarCommand::run_streaming() spawn child processes without applying creation_flags(0x08000000).

Impacted Operations & Binaries

Feature / Operation Trigger / Caller Binary Executed Visual Impact
Frame Extraction Ingest job (extract_frames) ffmpeg.exe Console window stays open for the entire duration of video extraction
GPS Telemetry Extraction Ingest job (extract_telemetry) bolt42.exe Brief console flash during telemetry parsing
GPX Extraction Ingest job (extract_camm_exiftool) exiftool.exe Brief console flash during CAMM metadata extraction
Video Probing Ingest job (probe_video_fast) ffmpeg.exe / ffprobe.exe Brief console flash during duration & stream check
Timeline Strip Project editor (start_timeline_strip) ffmpeg.exe Console flash while rendering thumbnail strip
EXIF Injection Tour upload (tag_photos_exif) exiftool.exe Console flash while writing coordinates & heading to JPEGs
Sidecar Diagnostics Diagnostics modal (probe_sidecars) All 4 sidecars Sequential console flashes during version checks

Resolution Plan

Add CREATE_NO_WINDOW (0x08000000) flag on Windows when constructing tokio::process::Command in SidecarCommand (crates/sb-core/src/media/sidecar.rs). Because all 19 call sites throughout the codebase route through SidecarCommand, this single-point fix resolves the issue across all features simultaneously while preserving pipe capture and streaming functionality.
